subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a persistent TUI accessibility profile, and which complete set of decorative Unicode and emoji output must it replace?
rationale: Source proves the user problem and implementation boundary, but the setting name, default, scope, and stable replacement vocabulary are durable product and configuration choices that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve full accessible profile
options.body: Add one documented setting and typed ASCII or text palette spanning tool summaries, statuses, selectors, separators, and upstream component themes.

options.title: Make ASCII the default
options.body: Remove decorative Unicode from normal TUI output for every user and avoid adding another persistent config key.

options.title: Defer the mode
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers can own a comprehensive accessibility contract and real screen-reader validation.

recommendation.title: Approve full accessible profile
recommendation.body: Add one documented setting and typed ASCII or text palette spanning tool summaries, statuses, selectors, separators, and upstream component themes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail connects this person to both the original TUI UI kit and centralized tool-display behavior.
